concern.concern: Step 1.1 says, 'Give X its natural finite CW structure with one vertex, core edges a,b,c, and 2-cells λ₂,λ₃'. Here X was defined as the union of two mapping cylinders: the common source circle c and the two target core circles are disjoint, so that actual space cannot have the asserted one-vertex structure with all three as core edges. The usual construction first includes the two connecting cylinder edges and then collapses their maximal tree to obtain the asserted presentation complex. That finite simple comparison is omitted from the claimed spine certificate.

original_concerns.reason: The union of the two mapping cylinders has three distinct circle vertices and two connecting interval edges. The missing maximal-tree quotient matters because this paragraph supplies a based simple-spine certificate, stronger than merely a group presentation. A finite tree contraction before the existing 2-cell slide preserves the full example and its torsion calculation.

required_own_edits.source_excerpt: Choose finite cell structures compatible with this map and the two degree maps, and take the unique vertex of $X$ as basepoint. In the resulting mapping-cylinder CW structure, each prism over a boundary-torus cell $\sigma$ pairs with its unglued face $\sigma\times\{0\}$; removing these pairs in decreasing cell dimension gives a finite sequence of elementary collapses onto $X$, fixing $X$ and its chosen basepoint. Thus this specific exterior-to-$X$ equivalence is simple. Give $X$ its natural finite CW structure with one vertex, core edges $a,b,c$, and $2$-cells $\lambda_2,\lambda_3$ attached by $r_2=a^2c^{-1}$ and $r_3=b^3c^{-1}$.
required_own_edits.proposed_replacement: Choose finite cell structures compatible with this map and the two degree maps, with circle vertices $v_c,v_a,v_b$ and cylinder edges $e_a:v_c\to v_a$, $e_b:v_c\to v_b$; take $v_c$ as basepoint. In the resulting exterior mapping-cylinder CW structure, each prism over a boundary-torus cell $\sigma$ pairs with its unglued face $\sigma\times\{0\}$; removing these pairs in decreasing cell dimension gives a finite sequence of elementary collapses onto $X$, fixing $X$ and $v_c$. Thus this specific exterior-to-$X$ equivalence is simple. The natural CW structure on $X$ has these three vertices, edges $a,b,c,e_a,e_b$, and $2$-cells with based words $e_a a^2e_a^{-1}c^{-1}$ and $e_b b^3e_b^{-1}c^{-1}$. The two connecting edges form a maximal tree. Contract it to obtain a based presentation complex $\overline X$: this contraction is simple, as can be seen by moving the loops and attaching paths at each terminal vertex across its connecting edge by cellular edge slides, then collapsing that edge with the now free terminal vertex. Each cellular slide is realized by an elementary expansion followed by an elementary collapse; the root $v_c$ is fixed. After the two contractions, $\overline X$ has one vertex, edges $a,b,c$, and $2$-cells $\lambda_2,\lambda_3$ attached by $r_2=a^2c^{-1}$ and $r_3=b^3c^{-1}$. Work in $\overline X$ for the following further simple changes.
